function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here are a few ways you can order a cake, depending on what you’re looking for:

| Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips |
|--------|----------------|--------------|------|
| **Online cake delivery services** | Nationwide delivery, custom designs, same‑day options | Visit the website or app, choose a cake, add personalization, checkout | Check delivery times & fees; read reviews for quality |
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often handmade, sometimes unique flavors | Call or visit the bakery, place an order in person or via their website | Great for supporting local businesses; ask about special dietary needs |
| **Supermarket bakery sections** | Convenient, ready‑made cakes, sometimes custom | Go to the bakery counter, pick a cake, or order a custom one | Good for quick orders; check for seasonal specials |
| **Specialty dessert shops** | Gourmet, artisanal, often vegan or gluten‑free | Browse their menu online or in‑store, place an order | Ideal for celebrations or unique flavor profiles |
| **Subscription services** | Monthly cake deliveries, themed boxes | Sign up on their site, choose a plan, receive a cake each month | Fun for regular treats or gifting |

### Popular Online Platforms (U.S. & Canada)

| Platform | Highlights | Link |
|----------|------------|------|
| **Goldbelly** | Curated selection from famous bakeries across the U.S. | https://goldbelly.com |
| **Etsy** | Handmade cakes from independent bakers worldwide | https://etsy.com |
| **Blue Apron** | Occasionally offers cake kits (DIY) | https://www.blueapron.com |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Quick delivery from local stores | https://www.amazon.com/fresh |
| **Instacart** | Delivery from local grocery stores & bakeries | https://www.instacart.com |

### Local Options (If you’re in a major city)

- **New York City** – *Magnolia Bakery*, *Baked by Melissa*, *Dominique Ansel Bakery*
- **Los Angeles** – *The Cake Shop*, *Baker & Cook*, *Martha’s Kitchen*
- **Chicago** – *Baker’s Dozen*, *The Sweet Spot*, *Cakes & Bakes*
- **London** – *The Cake Shop*, *Baker & Cook*, *Martha’s Kitchen* (UK)
- **Toronto** – *The Cake Shop*, *Baker & Cook*, *Martha’s Kitchen* (Canada)

### Tips for Ordering

1. **Check Delivery Times** – Some services only deliver on weekdays or have cut‑off times.
2. **Read Reviews** – Look at recent customer feedback for taste, freshness, and packaging.
3. **Ask About Allergens** – If you have dietary restrictions, confirm ingredients or request a gluten‑free/vegan option.
4. **Personalization** – Most sites let you add a custom message or design; do this early to avoid last‑minute changes.
5. **Payment & Refund Policy** – Make sure you understand the payment terms and what happens if the cake arrives damaged.

If you let me know your city or the occasion (birthday, wedding, corporate event), I can narrow down the best local bakeries or online options for you!
